- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or is weak (negative sentiment → model underreacts).
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term volatility; smooth out sharp forecast jumps.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 30-day horizon.
- If recent 18-day price range is narrow, model tends to overpredict; apply mean reversion bias toward recent average.
- Forecast should adjust downward if sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment over 3–5 days.
- Avoid over-optimism after high recent prices; model often peaks too early and then drops — reduce peak forecasts by 3–5%.
- If sentiment is strongly negative and price is falling, model often fails to recognize the trend — forecast should lag slightly behind true price.
